release.title: Consumers price index: June 2026 quarter
release.headline: The consumers price index (CPI) increased 1.5 percent in the June 2026 quarter and 4.1 percent in the 12 months to June 2026.

executive_summary.text: The consumers price index (CPI) rose 1.5% in the June 2026 quarter and 4.1% over the 12 months to June 2026 (index 1,359, June 2017 quarter = 1000).
Quarterly inflation of 1.5% compares with 0.9% in the March 2026 quarter and 0.5% in the June 2025 quarter.
Annual inflation of 4.1% compares with 3.1% published for the March 2026 quarter in the previous release, a change of +1.0 percentage points.

Tradables inflation was 4.9% over the year (2.7% in the quarter) and non-tradables inflation was 3.4% (0.6%); tradables inflation was higher over the year. Contributions of tradables and non-tradables to the headline are not published in the files used, so this does not say which contributed more.

By Stats NZ's published contribution to the quarterly change, Transport (0.82 percentage points) and Housing and household utilities (0.31 percentage points) contributed most while Miscellaneous goods and services (-0.01 percentage points) subtracted. Over the year, Transport (1.48 percentage points) and Housing and household utilities (1.07 percentage points) contributed most.
executive_summary.caveat: The 11 groups sum to 1.40 percentage points quarterly against a headline change of 1.49; Stats NZ calculates contributions from unrounded indexes.

context.text: Over the 40 quarters to June 2026, annual CPI inflation ranged from 0.4% (September 2016 quarter) to 7.3% (June 2022 quarter); the latest rate is 4.1%.
No previously published unadjusted all-groups index value changed in this release.

Stats NZ's published trimmed mean (30 percent trim) was 0.8% and its weighted median 0.4% for the quarter, against 1.5% for all groups. These are official Stats NZ measures published with the release workbook.

definitions: The consumers price index (CPI) measures the change in prices of a fixed basket of goods and services bought by New Zealand households. It is not a cost-of-living index for any one household.

Index numbers use a June 2017 quarter (=1000) base. Quarterly change compares a quarter with the previous quarter; annual change compares it with the same quarter a year earlier. They are different measures and are never drawn as one series. Official changes are calculated from the rounded published index numbers, as here.
Tradables are goods and services exposed to foreign competition; non-tradables are not. Non-tradables inflation is not core inflation.
notes: A group's percentage price change, its percentage-point contribution to the headline change and its share of the total movement are three different measures. Contributions shown are the percentage-point figures Stats NZ publishes (supplementary analytical information calculated from unrounded index numbers), so the 11 groups sum to the headline change only approximately.
Seasonally adjusted series are re-estimated every quarter and can be revised. Unadjusted CPI is not normally revised.

Stats NZ updates the basket and expenditure weights periodically and describes method changes in its price index methods updates. For the September 2026 quarter these include administrative data for long-distance bus fares. Stats NZ has also noted that a timing error in vehicle relicensing fees (a January 2025 increase applied as a catch-up in June 2025) raised annual inflation in the March 2026 quarter relative to when the change occurred.

Selected Price Indexes are a separate monthly release and are not monthly CPI. Quarterly CPI remains the official measure. Trimmed means and weighted percentiles shown are official Stats NZ measures from the release workbook; this dashboard does not define core inflation.
This page describes published statistics only. It makes no forecast and no statement about policy decisions.
